description: A Snowpark DataFrame is a PLAN, not a result. Measured against a live account with an identical Java handler: session.sql("INSERT ...") on its own runs NOTHING and the handler returns normally; adding .collect() runs it once; calling collect() TWICE runs it twice, because a plan is not memoised; count() is an action alongside collect(), so count() then collect() also runs it twice; session.table("missing") raises nothing until an action asks for rows; and an owner's-rights CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE returns normally with no action and is refused at the ACTION. Executing inside sql() - which this stub used to do - is the one divergence shape that HIDES: a handler that builds a statement and never collects does real work here and nothing on Snowflake, so the test passes locally and the procedure is a no-op in production. Converted 1:1 from scripting/SnowparkLazyPlanTest (now retired). The Java constructed Session and DataFrame objects DIRECTLY, which has no SQL surface; each claim is expressed here through a LANGUAGE JAVA handler doing the same calls, which is the shape the class's own javadoc describes as the live equivalent and goes through the real procedure path rather than around it. The one claim that changes shape is the last: the Java built a DataFrame over already-materialised rows with new DataFrame(resultSet), so the converted test makes the same point through a plan over a SELECT - repeated actions keep answering the same rows - which is the observable half of it.
